# Relations
The ICSC belongs to no bloc. We trade with everyone, carry everyone's messages, and owe no flag our soldiers. That neutrality is why the powers can stand to sit with us at one table, and why most UNISC peacekeepers wear our accent.
## The Powers - [bold]Three World Empire.[/bold] We fought them for our independence, and today their navy helps defend our space. The alliance is real and nobody pretends it is warm. [netlink="TWE Embassy" link="embassy.twe"] - [bold]United Americas.[/bold] The UA does not recognise the ICSC and calls our members secessionists. Their Marines were sent against us in 2148. We keep the channel open anyway. [netlink="UA Embassy" link="embassy.ua"] - [bold]Union of Progressive Peoples.[/bold] Courteous, careful, and like the others not ready to call us a nation. We talk about trade, shipping lanes and the safety of civilians. [netlink="UPP Embassy" link="embassy.upp"] - [bold]Central Confederation of Africa.[/bold] A rising power that knows what it is to be the junior partner. We find a great deal to discuss. [netlink="CCA Embassy" link="embassy.cca"]
## The UN and UNISC - The UNISC brokered the '51 New Deal that ended the Core Conflict. - Our citizens fill most of its peacekeeping ranks. Treat them as neutrals under the Conventions.
## On This Colony - Some frontier colonies stand on land held under an ICSC charter, often with facilities of the UA, the UPP and the TWE operating side by side. On such a world the charter is the law the Mission answers to, however thinly it is enforced. - A charter does not make the Mission a garrison, and it does not make anyone's quarrel ours. - Corporations on this world, Weyland-Yutani included, are guests of the colony like everyone else, whatever their land deeds say. - The Mission does not negotiate with armed groups. Anyone who lays down their weapons may come to the desk.
